1] This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR lodged at Crime No.233/2021 at Police Station Pithampur, District Dhar (M.P.) under Sections 363,
366, 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3/4(2), 5(L)/6 of the Scheduled Caste &
Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 as also for quashing the further proceedings pending in Special Case No.42/2021 before the Special Judge, Dhar on the ground that the matter has been compromised between the petitioner and the prosecutrix.

1 2] Shri Sanjay Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the date of incident is 21.05.2021 and the prosecutrix has already been examined in the Trial Court and she has not supported the case of the prosecution in any manner and she has also compromised the matter out of the court, and with the permission of her parents, the petitioner has also solemnized marriage with he prosecutrix, thus, it is submited that further continuation of trial would only be a futile exercise and will be sheer waste of precious time of the Court.

sentences.text: 3] Counsel for respondent No.2/prosecutrix has also submitted that the matter be closed and the petition may be allowed as the matter has already been compromised between the parties and the petitioner and respondent No.2 have also solemnized the marriage and out of this wedlock, they also have a girl child.
sentences._hearing_file: Ankit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: 4] Counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.
sentences._hearing_file: Ankit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5] On the last date of hearing, i.e. on 16/03/2023, the prosecutrix was also present before this Court along with the petitioner, and she had also submitted that she has no objection if the petition is allowed and had confirmed the factum of their marriage and a daughter being born out of the wedlock was also noted by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Ankit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: 6] Having considered the rival submissions, and on perusal of the documents filed on record and further taking note of the statement of the prosecutrix and her father recorded in the Trial Court, in which, they have not at all supported the case of the prosecution in any manner and has clearly given a clean chit to the petitioner, and further considering the fact that both the petitioner and the prosecutrix have solemnized the marriage and out of this wedlock, they also have a girl child, this Court is of the opinion that further proceedings against the petitioner would be only be a futile exercise.

sentences.text:
7] Accordingly, the petition stands allowed and the FIR registered at Crime No.233/2021 at Police Station Pithampur, District Dhar (M.P.) under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3/4(2), 5(L)/6 of the Scheduled Caste & Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and all subsequent proceedings arising out of the same in SC No.42/2021,
are hereby quashed.
